A: So, can we talk about the World Baseball Classic? I mean, wow, Venezuela just pulled off an epic upset against Team USA!

B: Right? I couldn’t believe it when I saw the score! Venezuela winning their first title ever is just incredible! 

A: Totally! They were leading 2-0 into the eighth inning, and I was thinking, “This is it!” But then, you know, Bryce Harper comes in with that monster two-run home run. I was jumping off my couch!

B: Oh man, same! I was like, “Here we go, Team USA is back in it!” But then, just when you think the game’s turned, Eugenio Suárez steps up and hits that clutch double. What a rollercoaster!

A: Right? It was like a scene straight out of a movie. And then the ninth inning just sealed the deal. I mean, Daniel Palencia shutting the door—what a performance!

B: Exactly! It’s like the whole world was holding its breath. I was convinced Team USA would pull through, but nope! It’s wild how they were, you know, the favorites and all, and they ended up with a second straight runner-up finish.

A: Yeah, and their lineup was stacked! I mean, you’ve got Aaron Judge, Bobby Witt Jr., Kyle Schwarber—how do they only muster three hits? It’s just mind-blowing!

B: It really is! I guess sometimes the pressure gets to you. I mean, they even had a nerve-wracking path to the semifinals. Losing to Italy? Yikes!

A: Right? They were so close to being knocked out after that—it’s just crazy how the tournament played out. Italy beating Mexico really kept them alive.

B: And can we talk about how Italy was like the Cinderella story? I mean, who would’ve thought they’d be taking down giants? 

A: Exactly! They were like, “Surprise! We’re here to crash the party!” It’s the beauty of sports, you know? Anything can happen!

B: For sure! I love that unpredictability. Makes it all the more exciting to watch. And now, with Venezuela taking the crown, I can only imagine the celebration back home.

A: Oh, it must be wild! I mean, this is history for them. Do you think we’ll see more momentum for baseball in Venezuela now? 

B: I hope so! I mean, this win could inspire a whole new generation of players. Who knows, maybe the next big MLB star is in Venezuela right now, dreaming big.

A: That would be awesome! I can already see the headlines: “Venezuelan talent taking the league by storm!” 

B: Haha, yes! And, you know, Team USA's manager suggested moving the WBC to the middle of the MLB season. What do you think about that?

A: Hmm, that could definitely shake things up! But I wonder how that would affect player availability. I mean, it’s one thing to play in the offseason, but mid-season?

B: Right? It’d be a whole different ball game. But, hey, if it keeps the competition fierce, I’m all for it!

A: Absolutely! Let’s see where they go from here. More surprises, more drama, and of course, more incredible baseball! 

B: You know it! Can’t wait for the next WBC.

Venezuela upset the Americans 3-2 to win its first World Baseball Classic crown
Venezuela is the champion of the 2026 World Baseball Classic after upsetting Team USA 3-2 in dramatic fashion in Tuesday night's title game.
Venezuela held a 2-0 lead into the eighth inning before Bryce Harper tied things up with a towering two-run home run in the bottom of the frame. But the game wasn't tied for long as Eugenio Suárez slugged a clutch double in the top of the ninth to put Venezuela back in front. Daniel Palencia then shut the door in the bottom of the ninth to seal the first World Baseball Classic title in Venezuela's history and USA's second straight runner-up finish.
Venezuela had to stage a comeback in the semifinals to beat Cinderella story Italy and set up Tuesday's showdown with Team USA, who won a tense 2-1 semifinal showdown against the Dominican Republic on Sunday night in Miami thanks to solo home runs from Gunnar Henderson and Roman Anthony.
The American bats were largely quiet against the D.R., and the story was the same in the title game as a powerhouse lineup that included Aaron Judge, Bobby Witt Jr. and Kyle Schwarber mustered only three hits in a disappointing showing.
